q22328.en: The maximum speed limit for a car on motorways is, as a rule, 130 km/h.

explain.short: On motorways (autostrade) the normal limit for cars is 130 km/h. Signs, rain or snow can change it, so the quiz says 'as a rule'.
explain.rule: Car limits: motorway 130 km/h, main extra-urban road 110 km/h, secondary extra-urban road 90 km/h, town 50 km/h. Vehicles up to 3.5 tonnes and motorbikes have the same limits; signs can change them.
explain.trap: 'ordinariamente' means 'as a rule / normally': it leaves room for exceptions, so the sentence is safe.

sceneParams.caption: Motorway, normal limit: 130 km/h

q22329.en: The maximum speed limit for a car on main extra-urban roads is, as a rule, 110 km/h.

explain.short: On main extra-urban roads (strade extraurbane principali, big roads outside towns with separate carriageways) cars normally may drive at 110 km/h.
explain.rule: Car limits: motorway 130 km/h, main extra-urban road 110 km/h, secondary extra-urban road 90 km/h, town 50 km/h. Vehicles up to 3.5 tonnes and motorbikes have the same limits; signs can change them.
explain.trap: 'ordinariamente' (as a rule) leaves room for the exceptions: rain, new drivers, signs.

sceneParams.caption: Main extra-urban road: 110 km/h

q22330.en: The maximum speed limit for a car on secondary extra-urban roads is 90 km/h.

explain.short: Secondary extra-urban roads (strade extraurbane secondarie, ordinary roads outside towns) have a 90 km/h limit for cars.
explain.rule: Car limits: motorway 130 km/h, main extra-urban road 110 km/h, secondary extra-urban road 90 km/h, town 50 km/h. Vehicles up to 3.5 tonnes and motorbikes have the same limits; signs can change them.
explain.trap: Do not mix 'principali' (110 km/h) and 'secondarie' (90 km/h).

sceneParams.caption: Secondary extra-urban road: 90 km/h

q22331.en: The maximum speed limit for a car in built-up areas is, as a rule, 50 km/h.

explain.short: In towns (centri abitati, built-up areas) the normal limit is 50 km/h. Signs can raise it up to 70 km/h on some roads or lower it.
explain.rule: Car limits: motorway 130 km/h, main extra-urban road 110 km/h, secondary extra-urban road 90 km/h, town 50 km/h. Vehicles up to 3.5 tonnes and motorbikes have the same limits; signs can change them.
explain.trap: 'ordinariamente' (as a rule) makes it right; with 'sempre' (always) it would be wrong.

sceneParams.caption: In town, normal limit: 50 km/h

q22332.en: The maximum speed limit for a motor vehicle up to 3.5 tonnes on motorways is, as a rule, 130 km/h.

explain.short: Motor vehicles up to 3.5 tonnes (cars, vans, light trucks) have the same motorway limit as cars: 130 km/h.
explain.rule: Car limits: motorway 130 km/h, main extra-urban road 110 km/h, secondary extra-urban road 90 km/h, town 50 km/h. Vehicles up to 3.5 tonnes and motorbikes have the same limits; signs can change them.
explain.trap: 'fino a 3,5 tonnellate' (up to 3.5 tonnes) means a light vehicle: it follows car limits.

sceneParams.caption: Up to 3.5 t on the motorway: 130 km/h

q22333.en: The maximum speed limit for a lorry up to 3.5 tonnes on main extra-urban roads is 110 km/h.

explain.short: A light lorry (autocarro, goods vehicle) up to 3.5 tonnes follows car limits: 110 km/h on main extra-urban roads.
explain.rule: Car limits: motorway 130 km/h, main extra-urban road 110 km/h, secondary extra-urban road 90 km/h, town 50 km/h. Vehicles up to 3.5 tonnes and motorbikes have the same limits; signs can change them.
explain.trap: 'autocarro' sounds like a heavy truck, but 'fino a 3,5 tonnellate' makes it a light vehicle.

sceneParams.caption: Light lorry, main extra-urban: 110 km/h

q22334.en: The maximum speed limit for a motor vehicle up to 3.5 tonnes on secondary extra-urban roads is 90 km/h.

explain.short: Vehicles up to 3.5 tonnes have the car limit on secondary extra-urban roads: 90 km/h.
explain.rule: Car limits: motorway 130 km/h, main extra-urban road 110 km/h, secondary extra-urban road 90 km/h, town 50 km/h. Vehicles up to 3.5 tonnes and motorbikes have the same limits; signs can change them.
explain.trap: 'secondarie' means the 90 km/h roads, not the 110 km/h ones.

sceneParams.caption: Up to 3.5 t, secondary road: 90 km/h

q22335.en: The maximum speed limit for a motorcycle in built-up areas is, as a rule, 50 km/h.

explain.short: In towns the normal limit is 50 km/h for everyone, motorbikes included.
explain.rule: Car limits: motorway 130 km/h, main extra-urban road 110 km/h, secondary extra-urban road 90 km/h, town 50 km/h. Vehicles up to 3.5 tonnes and motorbikes have the same limits; signs can change them.
explain.trap: 'ordinariamente' (as a rule) allows signs that change the limit.

sceneParams.caption: Motorbike in town: 50 km/h

q22336.en: The maximum speed limit for a car, where a specific sign is present on motorway sections with special features, is 150 km/h.

explain.short: On some modern motorway sections (for example with 3 lanes per direction and an emergency lane) the road owner may put signs allowing up to 150 km/h.
explain.rule: Signs can raise the limit: up to 150 km/h on some motorways and up to 70 km/h on some town roads. Without those signs: 130 km/h on motorways, 50 km/h in towns.
explain.trap: The key is 'in presenza di apposito segnale' (where a specific sign is present): without it the limit stays 130 km/h.

sceneParams.caption: Only with a special sign: 150 km/h

q22337.en: The maximum speed limit for a car, where signs are present on an urban road with special features, is 70 km/h.

explain.short: Some town roads are wide and safe (for example with separate carriageways). With signs, the limit there can be up to 70 km/h.
explain.rule: Signs can raise the limit: up to 150 km/h on some motorways and up to 70 km/h on some town roads. Without those signs: 130 km/h on motorways, 50 km/h in towns.
explain.trap: 'in presenza di segnali' (where signs are present) is the key: without signs it is 50 km/h.

sceneParams.caption: Town road with signs: up to 70 km/h

q22338.en: The maximum speed limit for a car on motorways in case of rain or snow is 110 km/h.

explain.short: Rain or snow make the road slippery and visibility worse, so on motorways the car limit drops from 130 km/h to 110 km/h.
explain.rule: With rain or snow (precipitazioni) the limit for cars drops: 110 km/h on motorways and 90 km/h on main extra-urban roads.
explain.trap: 'precipitazioni atmosferiche' means rain or snow falling: it lowers the motorway limit to 110 km/h.

sceneParams.caption: Motorway with rain or snow: 110 km/h

q22339.en: The maximum speed limit for a car on main extra-urban roads in case of rain or snow is 90 km/h.

explain.short: With rain or snow the limit on main extra-urban roads drops from 110 km/h to 90 km/h.
explain.rule: With rain or snow (precipitazioni) the limit for cars drops: 110 km/h on motorways and 90 km/h on main extra-urban roads.
explain.trap: 'precipitazioni atmosferiche' (rain or snow) lowers this limit to 90 km/h.

sceneParams.caption: Main extra-urban with rain: 90 km/h

q22340.en: The maximum speed limit for mopeds is 45 km/h.

explain.short: Mopeds (ciclomotori) are built to go no faster than 45 km/h, and that is also their legal limit on every road.
explain.rule: Slow vehicles have their own limits: mopeds 45 km/h, non-light quadricycles 80 km/h outside towns, farm machines and work machines with tyres 40 km/h.
explain.trap: 'ciclomotori' are mopeds, not motorbikes: their limit is 45 km/h.

sceneParams.caption: Mopeds: 45 km/h

q22341.en: The maximum speed limit for non-light quadricycles, outside built-up areas, is 80 km/h.

explain.short: Non-light quadricycles (quadricicli non leggeri, small four-wheel micro-cars) may drive at up to 80 km/h outside towns.
explain.rule: Slow vehicles have their own limits: mopeds 45 km/h, non-light quadricycles 80 km/h outside towns, farm machines and work machines with tyres 40 km/h.
explain.trap: 'non leggeri' (not light) and 'fuori dai centri urbani' (outside towns) both matter: the number is 80 km/h.

sceneParams.caption: Quadricycle outside towns: 80 km/h

q22342.en: The maximum speed limit for a car on any motorway is 150 km/h.

explain.short: 150 km/h is allowed only on special motorway sections with a specific sign. On a normal motorway the limit is 130 km/h.
explain.rule: Signs can raise the limit: up to 150 km/h on some motorways and up to 70 km/h on some town roads. Without those signs: 130 km/h on motorways, 50 km/h in towns.
explain.trap: 'qualsiasi' (any) makes it wrong: 150 km/h is only for some sections with signs.

sceneParams.caption: 150 km/h only with signs, not on any motorway

q22343.en: The maximum speed limit for a car on a main extra-urban road is 90 km/h.

explain.short: The normal car limit on main extra-urban roads is 110 km/h. 90 km/h applies only with rain or snow, or to new drivers.
explain.rule: Car limits: motorway 130 km/h, main extra-urban road 110 km/h, secondary extra-urban road 90 km/h, town 50 km/h. Vehicles up to 3.5 tonnes and motorbikes have the same limits; signs can change them.
explain.trap: 90 km/h is the limit for rain or for new drivers, not the normal one: do not mix them up.

sceneParams.caption: Main extra-urban road: 110 km/h, not 90
lines: Lower only with rain or new drivers

q22344.en: The maximum speed limit for a car on a secondary extra-urban road is 70 km/h.

explain.short: The car limit on secondary extra-urban roads is 90 km/h. 70 km/h is a limit for cars towing a trailer, not for a normal car.
explain.rule: Car limits: motorway 130 km/h, main extra-urban road 110 km/h, secondary extra-urban road 90 km/h, town 50 km/h. Vehicles up to 3.5 tonnes and motorbikes have the same limits; signs can change them.
explain.trap: The number is wrong: secondary extra-urban roads have 90 km/h.

sceneParams.caption: Secondary extra-urban road: 90 km/h, not 70

q22345.en: The maximum speed limit for a car in built-up areas is always 70 km/h.

explain.short: In towns the normal limit is 50 km/h. Only some special town roads with signs allow up to 70 km/h.
explain.rule: Signs can raise the limit: up to 150 km/h on some motorways and up to 70 km/h on some town roads. Without those signs: 130 km/h on motorways, 50 km/h in towns.
explain.trap: 'sempre' (always) is the trap: 70 km/h is only for some roads with signs.

sceneParams.caption: Town: 50 km/h; 70 only with signs
lines: 70 km/h: only some roads with signs

q22346.en: The maximum speed limit for a car in built-up areas is always 50 km/h.

explain.short: 50 km/h is the normal town limit, but not always: signs can raise it up to 70 km/h on some roads or lower it.
explain.rule: Signs can raise the limit: up to 150 km/h on some motorways and up to 70 km/h on some town roads. Without those signs: 130 km/h on motorways, 50 km/h in towns.
explain.trap: 'sempre' (always) is the trap; the correct word would be 'ordinariamente' (as a rule).

sceneParams.caption: Town: 50 km/h as a rule, not always
lines: Signs can allow up to 70 km/h

q22347.en: The maximum speed limit for quadricycles outside built-up areas is 70 km/h.

explain.short: Outside towns, non-light quadricycles may reach 80 km/h, not 70 km/h.
explain.rule: Slow vehicles have their own limits: mopeds 45 km/h, non-light quadricycles 80 km/h outside towns, farm machines and work machines with tyres 40 km/h.
explain.trap: The number is wrong: quadricycles outside towns have 80 km/h.

sceneParams.caption: Quadricycles outside towns: 80 km/h, not 70

q22348.en: The maximum speed limit for lorries in built-up areas is 40 km/h.

explain.short: In towns the normal limit is 50 km/h for all vehicles, lorries (autocarri) included. There is no special 40 km/h limit for them.
explain.rule: Car limits: motorway 130 km/h, main extra-urban road 110 km/h, secondary extra-urban road 90 km/h, town 50 km/h. Vehicles up to 3.5 tonnes and motorbikes have the same limits; signs can change them.
explain.trap: The number is wrong: in towns the general limit is 50 km/h.

sceneParams.caption: Lorries in town: 50 km/h, not 40

q22349.en: The maximum speed limit for a lorry with a total mass up to 3.5 tonnes on motorways is 120 km/h.

explain.short: A lorry up to 3.5 tonnes follows car limits: 130 km/h on motorways, not 120 km/h.
explain.rule: Car limits: motorway 130 km/h, main extra-urban road 110 km/h, secondary extra-urban road 90 km/h, town 50 km/h. Vehicles up to 3.5 tonnes and motorbikes have the same limits; signs can change them.
explain.trap: 'fino a 3,5 tonnellate' means car limits apply; 120 is not a standard limit.

sceneParams.caption: Lorry up to 3.5 t, motorway: 130 km/h

q22350.en: The maximum speed limit for a motor vehicle up to 3.5 tonnes on main extra-urban roads is 80 km/h.

explain.short: Vehicles up to 3.5 tonnes follow car limits: 110 km/h on main extra-urban roads, not 80 km/h.
explain.rule: Car limits: motorway 130 km/h, main extra-urban road 110 km/h, secondary extra-urban road 90 km/h, town 50 km/h. Vehicles up to 3.5 tonnes and motorbikes have the same limits; signs can change them.
explain.trap: The number is wrong: light vehicles have 110 km/h here.

sceneParams.caption: Up to 3.5 t, main extra-urban: 110 km/h

q22351.en: The maximum speed limit for a motor vehicle up to 3.5 tonnes in built-up areas is 40 km/h.

explain.short: In towns light vehicles have the normal 50 km/h limit, not 40 km/h.
explain.rule: Car limits: motorway 130 km/h, main extra-urban road 110 km/h, secondary extra-urban road 90 km/h, town 50 km/h. Vehicles up to 3.5 tonnes and motorbikes have the same limits; signs can change them.
explain.trap: The number is wrong: in towns the general limit is 50 km/h.

sceneParams.caption: Up to 3.5 t in town: 50 km/h, not 40

q22352.en: The maximum speed limit for any vehicle in built-up areas is 60 km/h.

explain.short: The general town limit is 50 km/h, not 60 km/h. Signs can raise it to 70 km/h only on some roads.
explain.rule: Signs can raise the limit: up to 150 km/h on some motorways and up to 70 km/h on some town roads. Without those signs: 130 km/h on motorways, 50 km/h in towns.
explain.trap: 60 km/h is not a town limit; the general one is 50 km/h.

sceneParams.caption: Town limit: 50 km/h, not 60

q22353.en: The maximum speed limit for a farm machine with tyres is 50 km/h.

explain.short: Farm machines (macchine agricole) with tyres are slow and heavy: their limit is 40 km/h, not 50 km/h.
explain.rule: Slow vehicles have their own limits: mopeds 45 km/h, non-light quadricycles 80 km/h outside towns, farm machines and work machines with tyres 40 km/h.
explain.trap: 'con pneumatici' (with tyres) is the same as 'gommata': the limit is 40 km/h.

sceneParams.caption: Farm machine with tyres: 40 km/h, not 50

q22354.en: The maximum speed limit for a work machine on tyres is 50 km/h.

explain.short: Work machines (macchine operatrici, e.g. road-works vehicles) on tyres have a 40 km/h limit, not 50 km/h.
explain.rule: Slow vehicles have their own limits: mopeds 45 km/h, non-light quadricycles 80 km/h outside towns, farm machines and work machines with tyres 40 km/h.
explain.trap: The number is wrong: 'gommata' work machines have 40 km/h.

sceneParams.caption: Work machine on tyres: 40 km/h, not 50

q22355.en: The maximum speed limit for a farm machine on tyres is 40 km/h.

explain.short: Farm machines on tyres (gommate) are slow and heavy, so their limit is 40 km/h.
explain.rule: Slow vehicles have their own limits: mopeds 45 km/h, non-light quadricycles 80 km/h outside towns, farm machines and work machines with tyres 40 km/h.
explain.trap: 'gommata' means 'on rubber tyres' (not tracks): the limit is 40 km/h.

sceneParams.caption: Farm machine on tyres: 40 km/h

q22356.en: The maximum speed limit for a work machine on tyres is 40 km/h.

explain.short: Work machines on tyres (macchine operatrici gommate) have the same 40 km/h limit as farm machines.
explain.rule: Slow vehicles have their own limits: mopeds 45 km/h, non-light quadricycles 80 km/h outside towns, farm machines and work machines with tyres 40 km/h.
explain.trap: 'operatrice' (work machine) and 'agricola' (farm machine) on tyres share the 40 km/h limit.

sceneParams.caption: Work machine on tyres: 40 km/h

q22357.en: The speed limit on motorways for those who got their licence less than 3 years ago is 100 km/h.

explain.short: New drivers (neopatentati, licence for less than 3 years) have lower limits: 100 km/h on motorways instead of 130 km/h.
explain.rule: In the first 3 years after getting the licence, the limit is 100 km/h on motorways and 90 km/h on main extra-urban roads.
explain.trap: 'da meno di 3 anni' (less than 3 years ago) means a new driver: 100 km/h on motorways.

sceneParams.caption: New driver on the motorway: 100 km/h

q22358.en: The speed limit on main extra-urban roads for those who got their licence less than 3 years ago is 90 km/h.

explain.short: On main extra-urban roads new drivers may go only up to 90 km/h, instead of 110 km/h.
explain.rule: In the first 3 years after getting the licence, the limit is 100 km/h on motorways and 90 km/h on main extra-urban roads.
explain.trap: Do not mix the two new-driver numbers: 100 km/h motorway, 90 km/h main extra-urban road.

sceneParams.caption: New driver, main extra-urban: 90 km/h

q22359.en: Travelling at high speed affects fuel consumption and environmental pollution.

explain.short: The faster you go, the more air resistance the engine must push against. It burns more fuel and makes more pollution.
explain.rule: High speed and sudden speed changes burn more fuel and pollute more. Smooth, moderate driving saves fuel.
explain.trap: 'incide' means 'has an effect on': high speed does have an effect.

sceneParams.caption: High speed: more fuel, more pollution

q22360.en: Sudden changes of speed lead to higher fuel consumption.

explain.short: Every hard acceleration burns extra fuel, and hard braking throws that energy away. Smooth driving uses less fuel.
explain.rule: High speed and sudden speed changes burn more fuel and pollute more. Smooth, moderate driving saves fuel.
explain.trap: 'brusche variazioni' means sudden changes: speeding up and braking hard.

sceneParams.caption: Sudden speed changes: more fuel

q22361.en: Speed in a bend affects the vehicle's road holding.

explain.short: In a bend the tyres must stop the car from sliding outwards. More speed means a stronger outward push and less grip left.
explain.rule: In a bend the tyres must hold the car on its line. The faster you go, the stronger the push outwards: the car can skid or even roll over.
explain.trap: 'tenuta di strada' means road holding (grip): speed in a bend changes it.

sceneParams.caption: Speed in a bend changes the grip

q22362.en: Too much speed in a bend can make the vehicle roll over.

explain.short: Too fast in a bend, the outward push can make the car skid or, especially if tall or loaded, tip over.
explain.rule: In a bend the tyres must hold the car on its line. The faster you go, the stronger the push outwards: the car can skid or even roll over.
explain.trap: 'può determinare' means 'can cause': it is a real risk, not a certainty.

sceneParams.caption: Too fast in a bend: risk of rolling over

q22363.en: Bends must be driven with the clutch pedal pressed down.

explain.short: With the clutch pressed the engine is disconnected from the wheels: you lose engine braking and control. Drive bends in gear.
explain.rule: In a bend the tyres must hold the car on its line. The faster you go, the stronger the push outwards: the car can skid or even roll over.
explain.trap: 'frizione abbassata' (clutch pressed) sounds smooth, but it means less control.

sceneParams.caption: Clutch down in a bend: wrong

q22364.en: The speed limit on motorways for those who got their licence less than three years ago is 110 km/h.

explain.short: New drivers have 100 km/h on motorways, not 110 km/h.
explain.rule: In the first 3 years after getting the licence, the limit is 100 km/h on motorways and 90 km/h on main extra-urban roads.
explain.trap: 110 km/h is the rain limit for all cars on motorways, not the new-driver limit.

sceneParams.caption: New driver on motorway: 100 km/h, not 110
sceneParams.it: patente da meno di tre anni

q22365.en: The speed limit on main extra-urban roads for those who got their licence less than 3 years ago is 110 km/h.

explain.short: 110 km/h is the normal limit for experienced drivers. New drivers have 90 km/h on main extra-urban roads.
explain.rule: In the first 3 years after getting the licence, the limit is 100 km/h on motorways and 90 km/h on main extra-urban roads.
explain.trap: 110 km/h is the normal limit, not the new-driver one.

sceneParams.caption: New driver, main extra-urban: 90 km/h, not 110

q22366.en: The maximum speed limit on motorways is, as a rule, 130 km/h for cars with a light trailer.

explain.short: A light trailer (carrello appendice, a small trailer for luggage) does not count as a real trailer, so the car keeps its 130 km/h limit.
explain.rule: A small light trailer (carrello appendice) does not change the car's limits. With a real trailer (rimorchio) or a caravan: 80 km/h on motorways, 70 km/h on other roads outside towns.
explain.trap: 'carrello appendice' is NOT a 'rimorchio' (trailer): the car limits stay the same.

sceneParams.caption: Car with light trailer, motorway: 130 km/h

q22367.en: The maximum speed limit on motorways is 80 km/h for cars with a trailer.

explain.short: A car towing a real trailer (rimorchio) is longer, heavier and less stable, so on motorways its limit is 80 km/h.
explain.rule: A small light trailer (carrello appendice) does not change the car's limits. With a real trailer (rimorchio) or a caravan: 80 km/h on motorways, 70 km/h on other roads outside towns.
explain.trap: 'rimorchio' (trailer) is a real trailer, different from a 'carrello appendice'.

sceneParams.caption: Car with trailer, motorway: 80 km/h

q22368.en: The maximum speed limit on motorways is, as a rule, 130 km/h for motorcycles.

explain.short: Motorbikes have the same motorway limit as cars: 130 km/h.
explain.rule: Motorbikes and camper vans up to 3.5 tonnes have the same limits as cars: 130 km/h motorway, 110 km/h main extra-urban, 90 km/h secondary extra-urban.
explain.trap: 'motocicli' (motorbikes) are not 'ciclomotori' (mopeds, 45 km/h).

sceneParams.caption: Motorbike on the motorway: 130 km/h

q22369.en: The maximum speed limit on motorways is, as a rule, 130 km/h for camper vans with a total mass up to 3.5 tonnes.

explain.short: A camper van (autocaravan) up to 3.5 tonnes counts as a light vehicle and has the car limit: 130 km/h on motorways.
explain.rule: Motorbikes and camper vans up to 3.5 tonnes have the same limits as cars: 130 km/h motorway, 110 km/h main extra-urban, 90 km/h secondary extra-urban.
explain.trap: 'fino a 3,5 tonnellate' is the key: light camper vans follow car limits.

sceneParams.caption: Camper up to 3.5 t, motorway: 130 km/h

q22370.en: The maximum speed limit on motorways is 80 km/h for a car towing a caravan.

explain.short: A caravan is a trailer, so a car towing one has the trailer limit: 80 km/h on motorways.
explain.rule: A small light trailer (carrello appendice) does not change the car's limits. With a real trailer (rimorchio) or a caravan: 80 km/h on motorways, 70 km/h on other roads outside towns.
explain.trap: 'traina un caravan' (tows a caravan) means a trailer: 80 km/h on motorways.

sceneParams.caption: Car towing a caravan, motorway: 80 km/h

q22371.en: The maximum speed limit on main extra-urban roads is, as a rule, 110 km/h for motorcycles.

explain.short: Motorbikes have the car limit on main extra-urban roads: 110 km/h.
explain.rule: Motorbikes and camper vans up to 3.5 tonnes have the same limits as cars: 130 km/h motorway, 110 km/h main extra-urban, 90 km/h secondary extra-urban.
explain.trap: Motorbikes are not slower by law: same 110 km/h as cars.

sceneParams.caption: Motorbike, main extra-urban: 110 km/h

q22372.en: The maximum speed limit on main extra-urban roads is 110 km/h for cars with a light trailer.

explain.short: A light trailer (carrello appendice) does not change the car's limits, so 110 km/h still applies on main extra-urban roads.
explain.rule: A small light trailer (carrello appendice) does not change the car's limits. With a real trailer (rimorchio) or a caravan: 80 km/h on motorways, 70 km/h on other roads outside towns.
explain.trap: 'carrello appendice' is not a 'rimorchio': no lower limit.

sceneParams.caption: Car + light trailer, main extra-urban: 110

q22373.en: The maximum speed limit on main extra-urban roads is 70 km/h for cars with a trailer for carrying boats.

explain.short: A boat trailer is a real trailer (rimorchio). Outside motorways a car with a trailer may go only up to 70 km/h.
explain.rule: A small light trailer (carrello appendice) does not change the car's limits. With a real trailer (rimorchio) or a caravan: 80 km/h on motorways, 70 km/h on other roads outside towns.
explain.trap: 'rimorchio per trasporto imbarcazioni' is a trailer: 70 km/h on roads outside towns that are not motorways.

sceneParams.caption: Car + boat trailer, main extra-urban: 70

q22374.en: The maximum speed limit on secondary extra-urban roads is 90 km/h for motorcycles.

explain.short: Motorbikes have the car limit on secondary extra-urban roads: 90 km/h.
explain.rule: Motorbikes and camper vans up to 3.5 tonnes have the same limits as cars: 130 km/h motorway, 110 km/h main extra-urban, 90 km/h secondary extra-urban.
explain.trap: Same number as cars: 90 km/h on 'secondarie'.

sceneParams.caption: Motorbike, secondary road: 90 km/h

q22375.en: The maximum speed limit on secondary extra-urban roads is 70 km/h for a car towing a caravan with a total mass of 900 kilograms.

explain.short: A caravan is a trailer whatever its weight, so outside motorways the car towing it may go up to 70 km/h.
explain.rule: A small light trailer (carrello appendice) does not change the car's limits. With a real trailer (rimorchio) or a caravan: 80 km/h on motorways, 70 km/h on other roads outside towns.
explain.trap: The '900 chilogrammi' (900 kg) detail does not matter: a caravan is always a trailer.

sceneParams.caption: Car + caravan, secondary road: 70 km/h

q22376.en: The maximum speed limit on motorways is 130 km/h for cars with a trailer.

explain.short: 130 km/h is for cars alone or with a light trailer. With a real trailer (rimorchio) the motorway limit is 80 km/h.
explain.rule: A small light trailer (carrello appendice) does not change the car's limits. With a real trailer (rimorchio) or a caravan: 80 km/h on motorways, 70 km/h on other roads outside towns.
explain.trap: 'rimorchio' (trailer) changes everything: 80 km/h, not 130.

sceneParams.caption: Car with trailer, motorway: 80 km/h, not 130

q22377.en: The maximum speed limit on motorways is 90 km/h for motorcycles.

explain.short: Motorbikes have the car limit on motorways: 130 km/h, not 90 km/h.
explain.rule: Motorbikes and camper vans up to 3.5 tonnes have the same limits as cars: 130 km/h motorway, 110 km/h main extra-urban, 90 km/h secondary extra-urban.
explain.trap: The number is wrong: motorbikes are not limited to 90 km/h on motorways.

sceneParams.caption: Motorbike on motorway: 130 km/h, not 90

q22378.en: The maximum speed limit on motorways is 90 km/h for camper vans.

explain.short: Camper vans up to 3.5 tonnes have the car limit on motorways: 130 km/h. 90 km/h is not their limit.
explain.rule: Motorbikes and camper vans up to 3.5 tonnes have the same limits as cars: 130 km/h motorway, 110 km/h main extra-urban, 90 km/h secondary extra-urban.
explain.trap: The number is wrong: light camper vans have 130 km/h on motorways.

sceneParams.caption: Camper van on motorway: not 90 km/h

q22379.en: The maximum speed limit on motorways is 70 km/h for a car towing a caravan.

explain.short: On motorways a car towing a caravan may go up to 80 km/h. 70 km/h is its limit on the other roads outside towns.
explain.rule: A small light trailer (carrello appendice) does not change the car's limits. With a real trailer (rimorchio) or a caravan: 80 km/h on motorways, 70 km/h on other roads outside towns.
explain.trap: 70 km/h is the trailer limit on other roads; on motorways it is 80 km/h.

sceneParams.caption: Car + caravan on motorway: 80 km/h, not 70

q22380.en: The maximum speed limit on motorways is 120 km/h for a car with a light trailer in case of rain.

explain.short: A light trailer keeps car limits, and in rain the car limit on motorways is 110 km/h, not 120 km/h.
explain.rule: With rain or snow (precipitazioni) the limit for cars drops: 110 km/h on motorways and 90 km/h on main extra-urban roads.
explain.trap: 120 is not a legal limit here: with rain it is 110 km/h.

sceneParams.caption: Rain on the motorway: 110 km/h, not 120

q22381.en: The maximum speed limit on main extra-urban roads is 100 km/h for motorcycles.

explain.short: Motorbikes have the car limit on main extra-urban roads: 110 km/h, not 100 km/h.
explain.rule: Motorbikes and camper vans up to 3.5 tonnes have the same limits as cars: 130 km/h motorway, 110 km/h main extra-urban, 90 km/h secondary extra-urban.
explain.trap: The number is wrong: motorbikes have 110 km/h here.

sceneParams.caption: Motorbike, main extra-urban: 110, not 100

q22382.en: The maximum speed limit on main extra-urban roads is 80 km/h for cars with a trailer for carrying boats.

explain.short: 80 km/h is the trailer limit on motorways only. On main extra-urban roads a car with a boat trailer has 70 km/h.
explain.rule: A small light trailer (carrello appendice) does not change the car's limits. With a real trailer (rimorchio) or a caravan: 80 km/h on motorways, 70 km/h on other roads outside towns.
explain.trap: 80 km/h belongs to motorways; on other roads outside towns the trailer limit is 70 km/h.

sceneParams.caption: Boat trailer, main extra-urban: 70, not 80

q22383.en: The maximum speed limit on secondary extra-urban roads is 70 km/h for motorcycles.

explain.short: Motorbikes have the car limit on secondary extra-urban roads: 90 km/h, not 70 km/h.
explain.rule: Motorbikes and camper vans up to 3.5 tonnes have the same limits as cars: 130 km/h motorway, 110 km/h main extra-urban, 90 km/h secondary extra-urban.
explain.trap: The number is wrong: 70 km/h is for vehicles with a trailer, not motorbikes.

sceneParams.caption: Motorbike, secondary road: 90 km/h, not 70

q22384.en: The speed of vehicles must be set so as not to obstruct traffic.

explain.short: Driving much slower than needed, without a reason, blocks the vehicles behind you. Your speed must keep traffic flowing.
explain.rule: Choose a speed that keeps traffic flowing and lets you slow down or stop to give way. Speed depends on road, traffic, visibility and weather.
explain.trap: 'intralcio' means obstruction: going too slowly can also be against the rules.

sceneParams.caption: Do not block traffic by going too slowly

q22385.en: It is compulsory to reduce speed and, if needed, stop at junctions to let through the vehicles that have priority.

explain.short: At a junction (incrocio) you must slow down and stop if needed to give way to vehicles that have priority.
explain.rule: Choose a speed that keeps traffic flowing and lets you slow down or stop to give way. Speed depends on road, traffic, visibility and weather.
explain.trap: 'all'occorrenza' means 'if needed': you stop only when someone has priority.

sceneParams.caption: Slow down, stop if needed, give way
lines: Give way to who has priority

q22386.en: It is compulsory to reduce speed and, if needed, stop from half an hour before sunset to half an hour after sunrise.

explain.short: That time window is when you must switch on your lights, not when you must slow down or stop. There is no such speed rule.
explain.rule: Choose a speed that keeps traffic flowing and lets you slow down or stop to give way. Speed depends on road, traffic, visibility and weather.
explain.trap: 'mezz'ora prima del tramonto' is the rule for LIGHTS, not for speed.

sceneParams.caption: Sunset/sunrise rule is for lights, not speed
lines: Not a duty to slow or stop

q22387.en: You are required to set your speed according to the engine's fuel type.

explain.short: Petrol, diesel, gas or electric does not change how safely you can drive. Fuel type has nothing to do with speed.
explain.rule: Your speed depends on the road, traffic, visibility, weather, load and your condition. It does NOT depend on fuel type, gearbox type or the speed of the cars behind you.
explain.trap: 'tipo di alimentazione' (fuel type) sounds technical but is not a factor.

sceneParams.caption: Fuel type does not decide your speed
lines: Fuel is not a speed factor

q22388.en: You are required to set your speed according to the speed of the vehicles behind you.

explain.short: You choose your speed from the road and traffic ahead, not to please the cars behind. If they are faster, they can overtake.
explain.rule: Your speed depends on the road, traffic, visibility, weather, load and your condition. It does NOT depend on fuel type, gearbox type or the speed of the cars behind you.
explain.trap: 'veicoli che seguono' (vehicles behind) do not decide your speed.

sceneParams.caption: Cars behind do not set your speed
lines: Do not speed up for it

q22389.en: You are required to set your speed according to the type of gearbox.

explain.short: Manual or automatic gearbox (cambio) does not change how fast you may safely drive.
explain.rule: Your speed depends on the road, traffic, visibility, weather, load and your condition. It does NOT depend on fuel type, gearbox type or the speed of the cars behind you.
explain.trap: 'tipo di cambio di velocità' (gearbox type) is a false factor.

sceneParams.caption: Gearbox type does not decide your speed
lines: Gearbox is not a speed factor

q22390.en: Speed must be moderate on stretches of road with poor visibility.

explain.short: If you cannot see far ahead (bend, hill, fog), a danger can appear suddenly. You must go slowly enough to stop in time.
explain.rule: Your speed must always be safe: slower where you cannot see far, in towns and near dangers, and right for your load and your physical state. Being in a hurry is never a reason.
explain.trap: 'a visuale non libera' means 'where the view is blocked'.

sceneParams.caption: Cannot see far: slow down
lines: Be able to stop in time

q22391.en: You must keep a speed that is not a danger for traffic safety.

explain.short: This is the basic rule: whatever the limit, your speed must never put you or others in danger.
explain.rule: Your speed must always be safe: slower where you cannot see far, in towns and near dangers, and right for your load and your physical state. Being in a hurry is never a reason.
explain.trap: No trap: this is the general safety rule.

sceneParams.caption: Speed must never create danger

q22392.en: You must keep a speed that lets you react safely to unexpected events.

explain.short: A child, an animal or a car can appear suddenly. Your speed must leave you time to brake or steer safely.
explain.rule: Your speed must always be safe: slower where you cannot see far, in towns and near dangers, and right for your load and your physical state. Being in a hurry is never a reason.
explain.trap: 'imprevisti' means unexpected events: you must always be ready for them.

sceneParams.caption: Leave room to react to surprises
lines: You can still brake in time

q22393.en: You must keep a speed suited to your own physical and mental condition.

explain.short: If you are tired, unwell or stressed, you react more slowly, so you must drive more slowly.
explain.rule: Your speed must always be safe: slower where you cannot see far, in towns and near dangers, and right for your load and your physical state. Being in a hurry is never a reason.
explain.trap: 'condizioni psicofisiche' means your body and mind state: tiredness counts.

sceneParams.caption: Tired or unwell: drive slower

q22394.en: It is the driver's duty to set the speed according to the vehicle's load.

explain.short: A heavy load makes the vehicle slower to stop and less stable in bends, so you must adapt your speed.
explain.rule: Your speed must always be safe: slower where you cannot see far, in towns and near dangers, and right for your load and your physical state. Being in a hurry is never a reason.
explain.trap: 'carico' (load) really matters: it changes braking and stability.

sceneParams.caption: Heavy load: adapt your speed

q22395.en: You must keep a speed set according to the time you have available.

explain.short: Being late is never a reason to drive faster. Speed depends on safety, not on your timetable.
explain.rule: Your speed must always be safe: slower where you cannot see far, in towns and near dangers, and right for your load and your physical state. Being in a hurry is never a reason.
explain.trap: 'tempo che abbiamo a disposizione' means how much time you have: hurry is not a factor.

sceneParams.caption: Being in a hurry is not a reason
lines: Speed depends on safety, not time

q22396.en: Speed must be moderate outside built-up areas.

explain.short: The law asks for moderate speed in towns and near dangers, not generally outside towns, where higher limits apply.
explain.rule: Your speed must always be safe: slower where you cannot see far, in towns and near dangers, and right for your load and your physical state. Being in a hurry is never a reason.
explain.trap: 'fuori dai centri abitati' (outside towns) is swapped: moderate speed is required inside towns.

sceneParams.caption: Moderate speed: in towns, not outside
